prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit the cell's ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins, from the PROTAC concept to the molecular basis of cereblon-mediated degraders

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B018 as the whole prize, to Crews, Deshaies and Handa. After the first round I still judge it the only shortlisted achievement that is both completely new and already consequential. Induced proximity changes the pharmacological logic from occupancy to event-driven removal of a target, and the chemistry is quantitative and testable: ternary-complex cooperativity, degradation kinetics, and structure-guided ligand and linker design. The concept has been reproduced by many independent groups for more than two decades, and the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide supplies the molecular explanation that unifies the glue strand with the PROTAC strand. The shortlist shows breadth of support, with B018 having the most top-three placements (five), and that supports my view only to the extent that each member's scientific reasoning holds, not as a count. Having read the chair's questions I would write the citation around the shared mechanism, redirecting the ubiquitin-proteasome system with small molecules, and not around drugs, so that it does not depend on any approval.
statement.case_against: The weakest points are the same as before and the first round sharpened them. No degrader drug is approved, so the clinical consequences are still promised more than delivered. Handa and Crews/Deshaies are different discoveries in the strict sense, so one citation spans two strands and leaves out Sakamoto, Ciulli, Gray, Ito and Kim. Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands are what made rational degrader design possible and I cannot call his omission comfortable. If the committee decides the glue strand must be a separate part, my single-prize configuration would not hold and I would then prefer the PROTAC concept alone over a forced combination.

responses.point: Linke proposes B029 (Liu alone) with B018 (Crews and Deshaies), and told me that Handa's cereblon work is a separate mechanism-of-action discovery that would stretch one citation across two achievements and four or more people.
responses.response: The objection is correct about discovery history: cereblon identification is biochemical target identification, not PROTAC design. But it does not persuade me to cut Handa, because the claim I make is about mechanism and not chronology. Thalidomide-type degraders are the one place where induced proximity was already a clinical fact, and Handa's work is what showed that. Dropping him leaves a prize about a concept with no approved example. My answer to the chair's question is therefore that the glue branch belongs in the citation, but only as three named people, and I would not argue it as a separate part. On Linke's pairing, I do not move to B029 as a second part. Liu alone is the cleanest base-editing attribution available, but the Nishida and Kondo claim stays open, and a second genome-editing prize six years after 2020 needs more than the cleanest wording.

responses.point: Chabes proposes B029 (Liu) with B018 (Crews and Deshaies), and says that a citation naming both Crews/Deshaies and Handa under one banner risks reading as arbitrary. If Handa is wanted, he asks that the citation say explicitly that it covers glue degraders and ask whether Deshaies still belongs.
responses.response: I accept his condition and have written the citation to say it: it names the PROTAC concept and the molecular basis of cereblon-mediated degraders. Deshaies still belongs, because he is co-author of the 2001 proof of concept with Crews and later stated the induced-proximity logic in the clearest form, so the question is whether Handa or Ciulli is the third name, not whether Deshaies stays. I also note that Chabes moved Komor and Gaudelli out of B029 to Liu alone under the chair's pressure, which confirms my view that B029 attribution is unsettled and is a reason to rank it as an alternative. His other concern, that no degrader drug is approved, I share fully, and it is my main reservation about B018.

responses.point: Somfai proposes B002 (Buchwald and Hartwig) with B029 (Liu) and, in reply to me, says that much PROTAC design is medicinal-chemistry optimisation and that cereblon is biochemical target identification that is hard to credit with PROTAC design in one citation.
responses.response: I agree that linker and ligand optimisation by itself would not merit a prize. The new chemical content I rely on is the induced-proximity principle: cooperative ternary-complex formation, which can give selectivity beyond the binary affinity of either ligand, and the hijack of an E3 ligase with a small molecule. These are physical-chemical points that can be measured and modelled, and I regard them as chemistry. On B002 I still do not see a principle that goes beyond the Pd(0)/Pd(II) manifold of 2010. The chair asks for one sentence of new principle and I would accept that the ligand-controlled amine coupling is more than an incremental step in synthesis. But it is not a new concept, and it would be a late prize for a method already rewarded in its main idea. I would not make Somfai's pairing of two mature-and-young achievements my configuration.

responses.point: Sparr agrees with B018 to Crews, Deshaies and Handa, but asks whether the committee is comfortable leaving out Sakamoto, who co-authored the first PROTAC demonstration, and notes that Ciulli's VHL ligands made rational design possible.
responses.response: Sakamoto's omission is a real attribution cost and I take the question seriously, but under a three-person cap the choice is between those who conceived the principle and those who made it practical. Crews and Deshaies led the 2001 work, and Sakamoto was the first author of a paper that came from the Crews laboratory, which is the usual separation that the committee has applied to trainees. Ciulli is the harder case, since he enabled ligand design after the concept was proven, and I keep him as the name I would swap for Handa if the committee insists on a PROTAC-only citation. Sparr's remark that the wording should rest on concepts and mechanisms and not on drug counts is now built into the citation.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a prize that joins the PROTAC and cereblon strands in one citation, or will insist that they are two achievements.
Whether Handa or Ciulli is the right third name, and whether Sakamoto's exclusion can be defended.

Whether the absence of an approved degrader drug makes the timing premature relative to a more mature B002 or B016. I have no fixed approval threshold, but an approval or strong late-stage data would settle the question for me.
Whether the Nishida and Kondo claim can be set aside, which would change my view of B029 as an alternative.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict or recusal need arises from my profile for any shortlisted candidate. My ties are to Arieh Warshel and the Uppsala ribosome and RNA community, and none of the credited names on the shortlist falls in those groups. Nothing in round 1 changes that.
